questions.question: Nirmal invested ₹1,380 at 3% per annum simple interest in a bank. What amount (in ₹) will he get after 3 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,380

Rate of Interest (R) = 3% per annum

Time (t) = 3 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × t) / 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

**Calculations:**

SI = (P × R × t) / 100

⇒ SI = (1380 × 3 × 3) / 100

⇒ SI = 124.2

Amount (A) = P + SI

⇒ A = 1380 + 124.2

⇒ A = 1504.2

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

⇒ A = ₹79,380

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Shan has ₹1,617 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Piyush and Manoj and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. questions.solution:

Total amount with Shan = ₹1,617

Piyush's investment grows to the same amount as Manoj's investment in 11 years and 12 years respectively.

Rate of interest (r) = 10% per annum, compounded annually.

A = P(1+(r)/(100))^t

**Calculation:**

For Piyush:

A = P(1+(10)/(100))¹¹

For Manoj:

Since both amounts are equal:

P(1+(10)/(100))¹¹ = (1617 - P)(1+(10)/(100))¹²

⇒ P × 1.111 = (1617 - P) × 1.112

⇒ P = (1617 - P) × 1.1

⇒ P = 1617 × 1.1 - 1.1P

⇒ 2.1P = 1617 × 1.1

⇒ P = (1617 × 1.1)/2.1

⇒ P = 770 × 1.1

⇒ P = ₹847

**∴ The correct answer is option (2): ₹847.**

questions.question: When the difference between compound interest, compounded annually, and simple interest for three years is ₹186 at 10% interest per annum, the principal is ₹_____.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference between compound interest (CI) and simple interest (SI) for 3 years = ₹186.

Rate of interest (R) = 10% per annum.

Time (T) = 3 years.

**Formula Used:**

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years = Principal × (R/100)² × [3 + (R/100)].

**Calculation:**

Let Principal = ₹P.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years = ₹186.

Using the formula:

⇒ 186 = P × (10/100)² × [3 + (10/100)]

⇒ 186 = P × (1/10)² × [3 + 0.1]

⇒ 186 = P × (1/100) × 3.1

⇒ P = 186 / (3.1 × 1/100)

⇒ P = 186 × 100 / 3.1

⇒ P = 6000

**The principal is ₹6000.**

Rate of interest = 10% compounded annually

Anil's time = 12 years

Ashok's time = 13 years

⇒ PAₙᵢₗ(1.1)¹² = PAₛₕₒₖ(1.1)¹³

Total principal: PAₙᵢₗ + PAₛₕₒₖ = ₹1617

⇒ PAₛₕₒₖ(2.1) = ₹1617

⇒ PAₛₕₒₖ = ₹1617 / 2.1

⇒ PAₛₕₒₖ = ₹770

⇒ PAₙᵢₗ = ₹770 × 1.1

questions.question: A bank offers 1.1% compound interest per annum calculated on a half-yearly basis. A customer deposits ₹7,745 each on 1 January and 1 July of a year. At the end of the year, the amount he would have gained by way of interest is ________. (Rounded up to the 2 decimal places.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate of interest (r) = 1.1% per annum (calculated half-yearly, so r/2 = 0.55% per half-year)

Deposit 1: ₹7,745 (deposited on 1 January, compounded for 2 half-years)

Deposit 2: ₹7,745 (deposited on 1 July, compounded for 1 half-year)

**Formula used:**

Compound Interest (CI) = Principal × (1+(r)/(100))^t - Principal

Where: Principal is the amount deposited

r is the rate of interest per period

t is the number of compounding periods

**Calculation:**

For Deposit 1 (₹7,745 for 2 half-years):

⇒ CI = 7745 × (1+(0.55)/(100))² - 7745

⇒ CI = 7745 × (1+0.0055)² - 7745

⇒ CI = 7745 × (1.011033 - 1)

⇒ CI = 7745 × 0.011033

⇒ CI = ₹85.43

For Deposit 2 (₹7,745 for 1 half-year):

⇒ CI = 7745 × (1+(0.55)/(100))¹ - 7745

⇒ CI = 7745 × (1+0.0055)¹ - 7745

⇒ CI = 7745 × (1.0055 - 1)

⇒ CI = 7745 × 0.0055

⇒ CI = ₹42.60

Total Compound Interest = ₹85.44 + ₹42.60

⇒ Total CI = ₹128.03

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
